title: Indian officials say Pakistan-based operatives allegedly infiltrated 13-14 WhatsApp groups of defence and paramilitary personnel, PTI reports
date_note: PTI says officials spoke on Monday 23 November; the report gives no date for the infiltration itself.
geo_basis: agency: PTI report datelined New Delhi; no unit location stated
summary: PTI, citing unnamed security and intelligence officials, reports that Pakistan-based Intelligence Operatives allegedly infiltrated about 13-14 private WhatsApp groups used by defence, paramilitary and defence-civilian personnel, likely using a spoofed or compromised Indian cellphone number, in what agencies call a targeted cyber espionage campaign. The officials say forces were told to audit the groups and remove unidentified members.
plain: Indian officials, quoted anonymously by the PTI news agency, say people they believe work for Pakistani intelligence secretly joined about 13-14 WhatsApp groups used by Indian defence and paramilitary staff.
exec: PTI reports officials saying spies allegedly joined staff WhatsApp chats unnoticed; unmanaged group chats can leak sensitive information.
action: According to PTI, officials told forces to audit and clean their WhatsApp groups, remove unidentified members and stop sharing official or classified information on social media.

validation.note: Only the PTI wire report, carried unedited by Free Press Journal, was read; it cites unnamed security and intelligence officials, no named agency or ministry. The attribution to Pakistan-based operatives is the officials' allegation, so actor is left empty. No second publisher found by search.

review.note: Compared title, 13-14 groups, officials' allegation, spoofed or compromised number, audit advice and date against the PTI report on Free Press Journal
